/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 20 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3005 (-49)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4880 (-69)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2374 (-85)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1566 (-2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 848 (-2)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the day on a mixed footing, as continued strength in the Pacific contrasted with softer conditions in the North Atlantic. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $625 to settle at $44,263. While the Pacific continued to build momentum on the back of healthy cargo volumes and sustained miner activity. The North Atlantic came under renewed pressure, offsetting gains seen elsewhere. C5 extended its recent upward trend, rising by $0.355 to $15.295, while C3 remained broadly stable with only a marginal decline of $0.127 to $36.323. In the Pacific, sentiment improved further as all three miners remained active alongside solid operator participation. Early fixtures on C5 were concluded around the $15 level by one miner before operators stepped in around $15.35, with post-index reports eventually suggesting business had reached as high as $15.50 from a miner. The South Atlantic also appeared relatively supported, with C3 holding steady throughout most of the session. A couple of fixtures were reported around the $36.45 level for 20/25 June and 25/30 June laycans respectively. Activity for index dates between 9/19 June was reportedly more limited, although post-index discussions suggested bids may have reached $36.75, albeit with details remaining somewhat unclear. Conversely, the North Atlantic softened notably, with a weaker trans-Atlantic fixture weighing on sentiment. This was reflected in the C8 index, which fell sharply by $5,613 to $46,875.
PANAMAX
The market extended its negative momentum into today, with both the Atlantic and Pacific softening at a faster pace. The BPI time charter average fell by $764 to close at $21,367. In the Atlantic, although a healthy volume of NC South America cargoes is providing some support to owners, pressure from available tonnage continues to weigh on rates. The Pacific is also seeing limited activity, with charterers remaining on the sidelines while a steadily growing tonnage list prompts owners to discount their offers. Volumes from Indonesia and Australia, which have driven the market in recent weeks, remain lacking and will need to recover soon for any meaningful floor to come into view.
SUPRAMAX
Another patchy day for the sector as downward pressure remained from the South Atlantic with limited fresh enquiry surfacing. The US Gulf lacked fresh impetus, but brokers felt fundamentals had changed little. The Continent-Mediterranean was finding a bit of upward pressure some said as better level of enquiry entered the mix, but fixing information was very limited. The continued downward slide was again seen from Asia with most areas attracting little fresh cargo and tonnage building up. Period activity surfaced however, there was talk of an ultramax open South China fixing about 3/5 months trading at $20,000. Also, it surfaced that the CL Spruce (64,181 2025) Qinzhou was placed on subjects at $22,000 for 5/7 months trading with Minmetal. The 11TC average finished to day down $33 at $19,789.

Atlantic
An ultramax was heard fixed from North Brazil to China at $17,750 plus $750,000 ballast bonus but no more details came to light. Elsewhere, the Sunny Bay (63,569 2022) Damietta 19 May was heard fixed with salt via Egypt to Mississippi River at $11, 500 to Pangaea and the Bahamas L (56,141 2012) Iskenderun 19 May was rumoured fixed with bulk cement via Eleusis to EC United Staes at around the mid $13,000s with Oldendorff, but the exact rate remained unclear.

Asia
The Ocean Makmur (60,445 2017) open Jakarta 30 May/5 June was heard to have been placed on subjects at $21,000 for a trip via Indonesia to China, but no more details surfaced. The Xin Hai Tong 60 (56922 2012) Surabaya 23/24 May was heard to have fixed a coal run coal in excess $20,000 from Indonesia to the Philippines. Also the HTK Lavender (61,494 20100) Samalaju 20/25 May fixed a coal trip Indonesia to China in the $18000s. Further north, the Sagittarius Honor (63,775 2025) Tianjin 25/28 May was heard fixed at $ 23,000 for a backhaul trip to West Africa, again further details were lacking.
HANDYSIZE
Building on the previous day, the market saw another subdued session, with limited activity reported. The BHSI fell by 2 points to 848, while the 7TC average dropped by $48 to $15,256. In the Continent and Mediterranean, market conditions remained soft, with little visible activity. In both the South Atlantic and the US Gulf, sources reported continued easing in bid and offer levels, as charterers and owners gradually adjusted their expectations lower. However, in Asia, the market remained supported, underpinned by tight prompt tonnage and a steady flow of cargoes.

Atlantic
The Karlino ( 39,035 2019) open Coatzocoalcos 23-25 May, placed on subjects for a trip delivery SW Pass to Cristobal with grains at $16,000 by J Lauritzen, but lacking further details.

Asia
The Poyang (39,790 2016), open CJK, was fixed for a trip to South East Asia with steel in the low $18,000s, while a 34,000-dwt open in the Far East was fixed to the Philippines at around $16,000, but further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Indonesia Announces New Centralised System for Commodity Exports

The Indonesian government has announced a new system to centralise commodity exports, including coal and palm oil, according to the President’s parliamentary address reported by newswires. The move is aimed at combating under-invoicing, which the government claims has cost the country around $900 billion over the past 34 years. A transitional period will begin on 1 June and by 1 September, all transactions, management responsibilities and authority are expected to be fully handled by state-owned enterprises under the oversight of Danantara, Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund.

While details on the mechanism and implementation remain unclear, the changes introduce uncertainty into the coal market and risk disrupting trade flows. Indonesia has previously made several attempts to control coal exports and prices. The new framework could give Jakarta greater control over both. As of 13 May, Indonesian coal exports stood at 166.9 Mt, down 5.9% year-on-year, vessel tracking data show.
